## kb_to_source

- Every normative sentence of the 21 documents of the three policies (hub, baseline, factors) and of the base/facet documents listed in source_to_kb was traced to a rule sentence, a factor ladder, a parameter, a measure, or the tool contract. Worked examples were re-computed (permit cases 100/90/41 days and 90.00/41.00/30.43; vacancy load 73 days -> 1.6 %; roof and building-age edges; indicated 1,294.9965 -> 1,295.00; capped 1,244.4432 -> 1,244.44; loyalty per-tier table; rental book 1,960 − 150) and all are correct.
- Additions / rewrites / omissions: none found.
- Cross-problem operational guidance ("if unmet, first call …", a named resolving tool or problem beside a state sentence): none. Each task tool name occurs only in its own hub.
- Opening world state written as policy fact: none (no document states this customer's vacancy, claims, permits or balances; all examples are marked hypothetical).
- Retired surface: the five overwritten base clauses relevant to this task are each carried as "no longer in force"; no undeclared clause is retired by the KB.

Policy-side notes (not KB defects; reported for the source layer):
- N1 `parameter_schema.renewal_offer_lead_days` reads "Days before expiration the renewal is billed", rendered faithfully as the row label in renewal_and_claims_frequency_values_bc20a803; the base clause that billed renewal installment 1 at the offer is retired and the paid-in-full rule bills nothing, so the source description is a residue of the retired clause.
- N2 `parameter_schema.vacancy_permit_rate_pct` ("prorated over the permit days") and base `formula: vacancy_permit_charge` are not named in `overwrite`; the facet vacancy_values_by_tier_a4c549d2 renders the description faithfully ("prorated over the permit days"), while the extended charge prorates over the charged permit days. On the visible surface the charged-days document resolves it explicitly ("The charged permit days are the day count used in the permit charge"), so no second answer results; the policy-side audit already recorded the same residue.
- N3 Two declared factors are defined over another factor's output in the source itself (claim_cause_weighting "weight … on the claims load"; late_payment_surcharge "late fees posted over the payment-history window"). Their documents necessarily name that quantity; this is the source's form, not a pointer added by the rendering.
- N4 (tool layer, outside the docs) the task tools round with Python `round()` rather than half-up; with 2-decimal inputs, as the docs require, this has no effect.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.** Every normative atom of the three extended policies (all tiers of all 15 factors, all three baselines, both prerequisites, all overwrites) and of the base policies they govern has an equivalent home in `docs/dwelling/`, and no normative claim lacks a source. First revision; no earlier revision exists.
